result: NEGATIVE -- no measurable speedup. 2,573 ms/token resident against 2,525 ms/token host-state, 1.9 percent SLOWER, within run-to-run noise.
what_was_built: GPU-resident decode state: activations, KV, router logits and top-k, expert selection offsets and sampling state kept on device across a token. Flag HAWKING_GLM_GPU_RESIDENT_STATE=1, default off, host path retained as parity oracle.
correctness: Parity holds. Resident output is bit-identical to the host-state path across several prompts, argmax/top-5/DSA top-k/expert choices all match, and incremental decode equals full replay. Verified by the controller after fixing a shader bug that had been masked by a skip path reporting green.
wiring_confirmed: gravity_glm.rs:1679 and :1704 route forward() and forward_at() through forward_resident when the flag is set. The benchmark exercised the resident path; this is not a misconfiguration.

why_it_did_not_pay.explanation: Resident state removes the readbacks that ATTENTION and routing forced. It does not touch the routed-expert path, which still issues three matvec_batch calls per layer each with its own commit_and_wait, nor the host dense lm_head. 538 matvec calls and 624 command buffers per token remain.
why_it_did_not_pay.conclusion: The prerequisite was necessary and is NOT sufficient. It removes the REASON attention forced readbacks; it collapses nothing on its own. The collapse is what pays, and it has not been attempted.

controller_claim_corrected.claimed: GPU-resident state is the prerequisite that unlocks the collapse ladder, and command-buffer collapse is impossible without it.
controller_claim_corrected.still_true: The dependency direction is real -- you cannot collapse command buffers while the CPU owns KV and computes attention.
controller_claim_corrected.wrong_implication: I presented it as though the prerequisite would itself move the number. It does not, and nothing in the ledger predicted it would: the buckets it addresses total ~8 percent plus part of a 23 percent bucket that is still dominated by expert dispatches it does not touch.
controller_claim_corrected.lesson: A necessary step is not a paying step. I should have predicted the size of this result from the ledger before running it, and said so.

what_this_changes: Nothing in the plan's ordering -- resident state still has to exist before the collapse. What changes is the expectation attached to it: it is scaffolding, not a milestone, and it should not be counted as progress toward TG20.
next: Collapse the routed-expert dispatch path, which the resident state now makes possible: three matvec_batch calls per layer into one, then across layers, toward one replayable token graph. Measure waits/token with the resident flag on via the cost ledger to confirm the remaining sync count is expert-dominated.
not_evidence_of: that resident state is useless -- it is a precondition whose value is realized only by the collapse it enables
